## What this measures

A **bubble column** is the simplest bubbly flow with a large-scale structure of its own: gas
rises, the liquid it displaces has to come back down, and in a closed column it does so along
the walls, setting up a circulation that in turn moves the bubbles sideways. This page runs one
such column with two codes that implement the *same* method:

- **[TBFsolver](https://github.com/cifanip/TBFsolver)** (Cifani et al., ["Highly scalable DNS
  solver for turbulent bubble-laden channel flow"](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0045793018303311),
  *Computers & Fluids* 2018) — the MPI+OpenMP Fortran code that introduced **multiple-marker VoF on moving
  blocks**: every bubble carries its own volume-fraction field on its own small box, so two
  bubbles that touch can never merge numerically.
- **`peclet.flow`** — the same container (one Weymouth–Yue geometric VoF field per bubble on a
  moving box, the union colour `max_k C_k` for density and viscosity, each bubble's own
  balanced-force surface tension summed into the momentum equation) on Kokkos, running here on
  one RTX 5080.

Both runs use **the same 128 × 96 × 64 cubic grid, the same 16 bubble centres, the same physical
parameters and the same closed-column forcing**, so every difference below is a difference of
discretisation, not of set-up.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this page exists
Colliding bubbles used to be *outside* peclet's rating: two markers that interpenetrated during
a collision produced, a few hundred steps later, a one-step velocity blow-up. Building this
benchmark is how that failure was found, diagnosed (not the force pairing it had been blamed on,
but a curvature estimate on sub-cell debris one marker leaves inside another) and fixed. The
section [The collision fix](#the-collision-fix) summarises it.
:::

## The case

Units: bubble diameter $D$, liquid density $\rho_l$ and gravity $g$ are 1. The bubbles are
case **E1** of Loisy, Naso & Spelt (*J. Fluid Mech.* **816**, 2017) — Archimedes number
$Ar = \sqrt{\rho_l(\rho_l-\rho_g) g D^3}/\mu_l = 29.9$ and Bond number
$Bo = (\rho_l-\rho_g) g D^2/\sigma = 2.0$, weakly ellipsoidal bubbles whose isolated rise
Reynolds number is about 31 — with density and viscosity ratios $\rho_g/\rho_l =
\mu_g/\mu_l = 0.02$ as in Bunner & Tryggvason (*J. Fluid Mech.* **466**, 2002).

| | |
|---|---|
| column | $8D$ tall (periodic), $6D$ between the no-slip walls, $4D$ deep (periodic) |
| grid | 128 × 96 × 64 cubic cells, $D/h = 16$ |
| bubbles | 16, a perturbed 4 × 2 × 2 array; void fraction 4.36 % |
| forcing | $(\rho - \langle\rho\rangle)\,g$ along the column, and **zero net volume flux** |
| run | $t = 0 \ldots 150\,\sqrt{D/g}$; statistics over $t \in [50, 150]$ |

The zero-net-flux constraint is what makes this a *batch* column. Without it (TBFsolver's
`flowCtrl 3`, the mean pressure gradient fixed at the mixture weight and the flux free), the
liquid descending along the walls feels an upward wall friction that nothing balances and the
whole column develops a steadily growing net upflow — measured at
$d\langle\rho u\rangle/dt \approx -0.0056$ before we switched. Both codes now remove the mean
velocity after every step (TBFsolver `flowCtrl 2`, `flow_rate 0`).

```{python}
#| code-summary: "Data loading + shared figure style"
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

DATA = "data"
plt.rcParams.update({"figure.dpi": 130, "font.size": 10, "axes.grid": True,
                     "grid.alpha": 0.3, "axes.axisbelow": True,
                     "figure.facecolor": "white", "savefig.bbox": "tight"})
C_PECLET = "#2a78d6"
C_TBF = "#e34948"


def ld(name):
    p = os.path.join(DATA, name + ".npz")
    return np.load(p, allow_pickle=True) if os.path.exists(p) else None


tbf = ld("tbf_closed_t150")
pec = ld("peclet_closed")
T0, T1 = 50.0, 150.0


def window(z, key="rise_speed"):
    m = (z["t"] >= T0) & (z["t"] <= T1)
    return z[key][m]
```

## Rise speed

The observable is the **drift velocity** — the gas-phase mean velocity relative to the
volume-averaged mixture velocity, positive upward — computed identically from both codes' fields.

```{python}
#| label: fig-rise
#| fig-cap: "Mean bubble drift velocity against time. Both runs start from rest from the same 16 centres; the shaded band is the statistics window."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 3.2))
ax.axvspan(T0, T1, color="0.93", zorder=0)
ax.plot(tbf["t"], tbf["rise_speed"], color=C_TBF, lw=1.2, label="TBFsolver (24 CPU cores)")
if pec is not None:
    ax.plot(pec["t"], pec["rise_speed"], color=C_PECLET, lw=1.2, label="peclet.flow (1 GPU)")
ax.set_xlabel(r"$t\,\sqrt{g/D}$")
ax.set_ylabel(r"drift velocity $/\sqrt{gD}$")
ax.legend(loc="lower right")
plt.show()

for name, z in (("TBFsolver", tbf), ("peclet.flow", pec)):
    if z is None:
        continue
    w = window(z)
    print(f"{name:12s} mean drift over [{T0:.0f},{T1:.0f}] = {w.mean():.4f} +- {w.std():.4f}  "
          f"(Re = {w.mean() * 29.9 / np.sqrt(0.98):.1f})")
```

## The column's structure

```{python}
#| label: fig-profiles
#| fig-cap: "Plane-averaged void fraction (left) and liquid velocity along the column (right; positive = downward) across the wall-normal direction, averaged over the statistics window."
fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.5, 3.2))
for z, c, lab in ((tbf, C_TBF, "TBFsolver"), (pec, C_PECLET, "peclet.flow")):
    if z is None:
        continue
    m = (z["t"] >= T0) & (z["t"] <= T1)
    y = z["y"]
    axs[0].plot(y, z["alpha_y"][m].mean(axis=0), color=c, label=lab)
    axs[1].plot(y, z["u_liq_y"][m].mean(axis=0), color=c, label=lab)
axs[0].set_xlabel("$y/D$"); axs[0].set_ylabel(r"void fraction $\langle\alpha\rangle$")
axs[1].set_xlabel("$y/D$"); axs[1].set_ylabel(r"liquid velocity $/\sqrt{gD}$")
axs[0].legend()
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

## Conservation

```{python}
#| label: fig-volume
#| fig-cap: "Relative change of the total gas volume. peclet's markers conserve their volume to round-off by construction — debris and sub-threshold residue are returned to the bubble they came from; TBFsolver deletes fragments and satellites and does not return them."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 3.0))
ax.plot(tbf["t"], tbf["gas_volume"] / tbf["gas_volume"][0] - 1, color=C_TBF, label="TBFsolver")
if pec is not None:
    v = pec["marker_volume_total"]
    ax.plot(pec["t"], v / v[0] - 1, color=C_PECLET, label="peclet.flow (sum of markers)")
ax.set_xlabel(r"$t\,\sqrt{g/D}$"); ax.set_ylabel("relative gas volume change")
ax.legend(); plt.show()
```

#| label: tbl-transient

## The collision fix

When two markers overlap, the Weymouth–Yue advection of each one leaves **sub-cell debris** in
cells the other bubble fills: volume fractions of order $10^{-8}$ to $10^{-3}$, strung out along the
rim of the contact lens. Every such cell passes the "is this interfacial?" test, so the
height-function cascade gives it a curvature — and over a debris cell nothing in the stencil is a
real interface, so that curvature is garbage: values of 273 and −428 per cell were measured where the
bubble's own curvature is about 0.4 per cell. Multiplied by $\sigma\nabla C_k$, it produced the one-step blow-up.
The balanced-force pairing of the per-marker forces with the union colour, which had been blamed, is
exact for a constant curvature and was not the cause.

The fix has three parts, all inside the block container:

- **Debris removal with exact return.** After every advection, a marker's cells that are interfacial
  but have no cell above $C = \tfrac12$ within two cells are cleared, and their volume goes back to
  the same marker's genuine interface, weighted by $C(1-C)$. Values below the wisp threshold
  ($10^{-8}$) are cleared the same way. Every marker's volume is conserved to round-off
  ($\le 2\times10^{-14}$ relative over thousands of steps). TBFsolver instead deletes fragments and
  does not return them.
- **A curvature bound** $|\kappa| \le 1/\Delta_{\min}$ per cell, active only for block markers, as
  a backstop for any stencil the removal misses.
- **A capillary time-step bound for the gas–gas contact.** Where two markers overlap, a phantom
  interface separates two gas regions, so the capillary limit is set by the gas density rather
  than the liquid's. The bound switches on only while markers overlap.

A static non-overlapping bubble is unchanged. A two-bubble shear collision that blew up at step
2910 now completes. The bubbly channel that died at step 10 706 runs past 13 000 steps with
volumes conserved to $2\times10^{-14}$. MPI runs at 1, 2 and 4 ranks are bitwise identical. The
design note, with every measured gate, is
[`doc/vof_overlap_design.md`](https://github.com/computational-chemical-engineering/peclet-flow/blob/main/doc/vof_overlap_design.md)
in `peclet.flow`.

## Reproduce this

```bash
# the case, shared by both codes
python scripts/case.py
# TBFsolver (patched to read explicit bubble centres: tbfsolver/bubblePositions.patch)
python scripts/make_tbf_case.py && cp -r tbfsolver/case tbfsolver/run
(cd tbfsolver/run && OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 mpirun -np 8 --bind-to none ./TBFsolver > run.log)
python scripts/tbf_read.py tbfsolver/run --out data/tbf_closed_t150.npz
# peclet.flow
python scripts/run_peclet.py --out peclet/run
python scripts/peclet_reduce.py peclet/run --out data/peclet_closed.npz --log peclet/run.log
```
